subject: Business Models
title: Territory Rights
description: A fast breakdown of Territory Rights for builders.

hook.text: You buy a Subway franchise. Then Subway opens another location 2 blocks away. Your sales drop 30%.

buildup.text: Territory rights define the geographic area where no other franchisee can operate the same brand.

discovery.text: Exclusive territories protect franchisees. Non-exclusive ones let the franchisor saturate an area for more fees.

twist.text: Subway infamously over-saturated markets. At one point, there were more Subways than McDonald's in the US.

climax.text: Territory disputes are among the most common franchise lawsuits. This clause matters enormously.

punchline.text: No territory protection means competing with your own brand. Read the contract.

quiz.question: What problem does territory exclusivity solve?
options: Preventing brand cannibalization from nearby same-brand locations
